lines.text: It's 37 out. Why is my windshield frozen?
That 37 is the air, measured about four feet up.
Your glass is lying back, staring straight up at the night sky.
It's losing heat. Everything glows invisible heat, and a clear sky sends back barely any.
So the glass drops below freezing while the air stays above it.
My car is colder than the weather?
Yep. Then water vapor touches the glass and turns straight into ice.
So my car stared at space all night and froze. Relatable.
Your car has a better night routine than you.
Then why is my neighbor's car totally clear?
Carport. That roof is warmer than the sky, so it sends heat back down.
Clouds do the same thing. A blanket for your car.
So I park under his carport. Got it.
Or a tree. And now you know.
